angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 17,051,607 km at 65.70 pc = 3.47 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Baines et al. (2018), AJ 155, 30, HD 215182: the Hipparcos (van Leeuwen 2007) parallax the radius was computed with (Table 1), 15.22 +/- 0.71 mas, inverted (https://doi.org/10.3847/1538-3881/aa9d8b): 65.703 +/- 3.065 pc; Gaia DR3 parallax 16.6308 +/- 0.7047 mas (same row, RUWE 10.19), 23.6 standard errors, is not used
radiusSource: Radius 24.51 +/- 1.21 solar radii from Baines et al. Mass 3.51 +/- 0.13 solar masses from Baines et al. (2018), AJ 155, 30, HD 215182: mass 3.51 +/- 0.13 solar masses (Table 6), from the PARAM Bayesian fit to PARSEC isochrones at the measured temperature; the paper calls its masses estimates only (https://doi.org/10.3847/1538-3881/aa9d8b); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 4970 +/- 65 K from Baines et al. (2018), AJ 155, 30, HD 215182: effective temperature 4970 +/- 65 K (Table 5), from the angular diameter and the bolometric flux of the SED fit (https://doi.org/10.3847/1538-3881/aa9d8b). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Baines et al. (2018), AJ 155, 30, HD 215182: effective temperature 4970 +/- 65 K (Table 5), from the angular diameter and the bolometric flux of the SED fit (https://doi.org/10.3847/1538-3881/aa9d8b)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/matar.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 2.205, rounded to two decimals

objectTypeSource: SIMBAD, * eta Peg: main object type SB*, Spectroscopic Binary
projectedRotationSpeedSource: SIMBAD, * eta Peg: projected rotation speed 1.8 km/s, the measurement SIMBAD prefers (2008AJ....135..209M)

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's measured spectrum (Pulkovo spectrophotometric catalogue, table 5 (320-1080 nm, 2.5 nm steps, 10 nm resolution, absolute flux in W m^-2 m^-1)) (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
